searchText: maybe stupid q: why is rlpx using ecies and not just have users sign their p2p messages? is it useful for anything beyond integrity of messages? the encryption is broken iirc? could an adversary impersonate a peer and cause reputation drops? There's no reputation system in el land Because of this, yeah iirc the encryption is broken ah i understand that it's not part of the spec but don't node impls disconnect peers that send "bad" msgs? i.e. if you can impersonate others can you not force disconnects? I think we are very lenient with peers sending bad msgs ok, context is im thinking of searchers going pvp with each other You might be onto something, if you spoof a message that is too large, you might be able to make geth disconnect the peer ugh 🙂 let's move to dm NVM - you recover the _session secret_ not the _peer's secret_, so you can only spoof msgs for that specific session so shouldn't matter perhaps. I think? I thought the opposite -- that you were strict and only binary in good/bad. Disconnect if do bad thing. But also ephemeral -- don't remember about past bad behavior that led to disconnects previously Well yeah, but we're pretty lenient in what we consider bad, so sending bad blocks for example wouldn't lead to a disconnect

excerpts.content: maybe stupid q: why is rlpx using ecies and not just have users sign their p2p messages? is it useful for anything beyond integrity of messages? the encryption is broken iirc?

excerpts.content: could an adversary impersonate a peer and cause reputation drops?

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: There's no reputation system in el land

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: Because of this, yeah iirc the encryption is broken

excerpts.author: gakonst
excerpts.content: ah i understand that it's not part of the spec but don't node impls disconnect peers that send "bad" msgs?

excerpts.author: gakonst
excerpts.content: i.e. if you can impersonate others can you not force disconnects?

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: I think we are very lenient with peers sending bad msgs

excerpts.author: gakonst
excerpts.content: ok, context is im thinking of searchers going pvp with each other

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: You might be onto something, if you spoof a message that is too large, you might be able to make geth disconnect the peer

excerpts.author: gakonst
excerpts.content: NVM - you recover the _session secret_ not the _peer's secret_, so you can only spoof msgs for that specific session so shouldn't matter perhaps. I think?

excerpts.author: djrtwo
excerpts.content: I thought the opposite -- that you were strict and only binary in good/bad. Disconnect if do bad thing. But also ephemeral -- don't remember about past bad behavior that led to disconnects previously

excerpts.author: mariusvanderwijden
excerpts.content: Well yeah, but we're pretty lenient in what we consider bad, so sending bad blocks for example wouldn't lead to a disconnect
